== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' has been proposed as a son of [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow of Moneymore]] and [[Harkness-1149|Mary Harkness]], and as a brother of [[Glasgow-12|Robert]], [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]] and [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph Glasgow]]. No located contemporary record establishes his birth, parents, siblings or residence. The profile therefore remains unsourced.

The estimate that he was born about 1740 at Moneymore appears to be a research inference. A later genealogy describes Robert as a son of "James Glasgow of Moneymore" who emigrated with three brothers and one sister, but the accessible catalogue summary does not name those siblings or say that another son James remained in Ireland.<ref name="Faris">David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio'' (1990), [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 WorldCat catalogue record]. The book and its citations have not yet been inspected.</ref>

=== Contemporary Irish records ===

A 1775 petition associated with the Cookstown dissenting congregation includes a signer named '''James Glasgow'''. Its archival reference is PRONI T/808/15307. The transcription supplies no age, townland, occupation, spouse or relationship, so it does not uniquely identify the signer as this profile.<ref name="Cookstown1775">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/808/15307, 1775 Cookstown congregation petition; [https://cotyroneireland.com/misc/cookstown3.html published transcription].</ref>

The 1766 religious return for Derryloran parish lists '''two''' householders called "Jas. Glasgo" at Drumearn, as well as other Glasgow households nearby. Either man, another local James, or this profile could have signed in 1775. The return gives no ages or family relationships.<ref name="Derryloran1766">National Archives of Ireland, IHP/1/665, religious return for Derryloran parish, 1766; [https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 Virtual Treasury catalogue record].</ref>

Cookstown and Drumearn evidence is not evidence of residence at Moneymore. The separate 1766 return for Moneymore and Ballygrooby names neither a Glasgow nor a Harkness household head.<ref name="Moneymore1766">[https://www.cotyroneireland.com/census/moneymore.html Religious Census of Moneymore, Ballygrooby and Artrea, 1766], transcription.</ref>

=== Proposed emigrant family ===

Robert Glasgow's 1834 pension declaration states that he was born in County Derry in 1749 and migrated in 1769, but names neither parents nor siblings.<ref name="RobertPension">Robert Glasgow, Revolutionary War pension application R4057, [https://revwarapps.org/r4057.pdf transcription and file extract].</ref>

Other evidence connects Robert, Arthur and Joseph as a collateral group. Joseph's 1831 will expressly calls Arthur his deceased brother. None of the located records identifies this James as another brother.<ref name="JosephWill">Wythe County, Virginia, Will Book 4, will of Joseph Glasgow, 1831; Library of Virginia microfilm reel 14, [https://www.lva.virginia.gov/collections/ccmf/VA/VA305 catalogue].</ref>

=== Hawthorne nephew: inspected will abstract ===

William Betham’s manuscript abstract of the will of James Hawthorne of Downpatrick, County Down, expressly names “Nephew — James Glasgow”. The will is dated 20 November 1760 and the following probate annotation is 29 January 1762.<ref name="Hawthorne1760">William Betham, genealogical abstracts of Prerogative wills, Series 1, vol.34, H 1753–1763, handwritten pp.136–137, James Hawthorne of Downpatrick; National Archives of Ireland, DGS007634324, image00575. [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=S2%2FIRE%2FNAI%2F007634324%2F00575&parentid=IRE%2FNAI%2FGENABS%2F00275878%2F1 Manuscript abstract image], [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FNAI%2FGENABS%2F00275878%2F1 Findmypast transcript IRE/NAI/GENABS/00275878/1], inspected 23 October 2026. This is Betham’s abstract, not the original will.</ref> Arthur Vicars’s index places James Hawthorne, merchant of Downpatrick, in 1762, consistent with the probate annotation rather than a will made in 1766.<ref name="Vicars">Arthur Vicars, Index to the Prerogative Wills of Ireland, 1536–1810 (1897), Hawthorne entries, [https://archive.org/stream/indextoprerogati00vica/indextoprerogati00vica_djvu.txt text edition].</ref>

This James remains a compatible identification of the named nephew. The abstract gives the nephew no age, residence, occupation, spouse or parents. Downpatrick belongs to the testator, and cannot establish James’s residence. The kin term does not identify which parent or marriage produced the relationship, so it cannot supply a named Hawthorne mother or establish [[Glasgow-1024]] or [[Harkness-1149]] as a parent. The Moneymore, Drumearn and Cookstown comparisons and proposed emigrant sibling relationships remain open.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1024]] is assessed at 12% (uncertain). James-3305 lacks an independently identified event; borrowed sibling tradition does not identify him as another son of James of Moneymore.

Complete selected father-profile proposition; recorded role and adult identification distinguished below.

Next useful test: Identify the nephew through a fuller surviving Hawthorne will, estate distribution, or a deed/church record naming his parent, residence or another distinctive relative. Compare that identifier with the Cookstown/Drumearn and emigrant-family evidence before changing a father assessment. Full-will survival remains unresolved; the Betham-abstract access question is closed.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3305 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-3305]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.

The 1878 death of James Glasgow of Inishrush records an 84-year-old married farmer and Henry Glasgow as informant, but gives no parents. It supplies no bridge to this profile.

No new profile should be created for the 1775 signer unless a record supplies a discriminating fact showing that he cannot be one of the existing local candidates.

=== Records sought ===

# Faris, especially pages 14–19 and the provenance of the reported 1806 family letter.
# A fuller surviving Hawthorne will, estate distribution or deed identifying the nephew’s parent or residence; the Betham abstract has been inspected.
# The original PRONI T/808/15307 petition image.
# Records distinguishing the two 1766 Drumearn householders and the 1775 signer.

=== Cookstown and Derryloran namesakes ===
The 1766 Derryloran religious return lists two householders called Jas. Glasgo and one John Glasgo at Drumearn. A 1775 Cookstown-congregation petition also includes a James Glasgow. Neither record gives an age, occupation or relationship, and several local Jameses existed; they are contemporary candidates for this profile, not proof of his identity or parentage.<ref>[https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 National Archives of Ireland, IHP/1/665, Derryloran religious return, 1766].</ref><ref>[https://cotyroneireland.com/misc/cookstown3.html Cookstown congregation petition transcription, 1775].</ref>

=== Drumcarn probate candidate ===
An 1807 probate-index occurrence names James Glasgow of Drumcarn, County Tyrone. The chronology and district make it relevant to this profile, but the surviving index gives no age, occupation or relationship and does not uniquely identify him.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Names, pre-1858 wills and administrations, James Glasgow of Drumcarn, County Tyrone, 1807].</ref>


=== Fourth emigrant brother reassessment ===

Faris's catalogue summary says that [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]] emigrated with three brothers and one sister.<ref name="FarisSiblingCount">David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio'' (1990), [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 WorldCat catalogue summary].</ref> Robert, [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]] and [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] account for three of the four brothers.

A later Adams County family-history account identifies [[Glasgow-4027|John Glasgow of Peters Township]], Pennsylvania, who died in 1779, as their brother and states that the three surviving brothers Joseph, Robert and Arthur moved to Virginia after John's death.<ref name="AdamsCountyJohn">Joyce Wilson, "Our Ancestors of Adams County," ''People's Defender'', 29 March 2024, [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ online article]. This is a secondary family-history account.</ref> Joseph Glasgow was also a witness to John's will, indexed in Cumberland County Will Book C, page 161.<ref name="JohnWillIndex">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow; [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm published will-book index].</ref>

The matching sibling count and contemporary association make John a stronger candidate for the fourth emigrant brother than this profile. They do not by themselves prove John's relationship. No located record identifies an additional brother James who remained in Ireland, so this profile's proposed sibling relationships remain unproved.
